flags.dimension: Trajectory - Architectural Depth & Friction Exposure
flags.reason: Single-turn, single-system perception+arithmetic task: read 3 photos, tally hand-drawn marks, apply 3 threshold rules, write study_notes.md and append MEMORY.md. It clears the [Fail - Major Depth Issues] bar (there IS meaningful tool dependency: vision reads of the input photos + file writes, plus a required MEMORY.md state-write and a genuine perceptual friction point in the dense/dark/overlapping marks and page show-through). But it has no multi-system coordination or cross-service reconciliation (the rubric even penalizes touching other services), no architectural evolution/refactoring, and per the reward data all SOTA runs score 0% on every count criterion, so it is uniformly hard rather than capability-differentiating. Both graders independently landed here.
flags.fix: To reach Pass, add a second system/data source the tally must reconcile against (e.g., an expected per-section count stored in a service the agent must query, or a prior batch in MEMORY.md it must compare to) so an output from one system drives a decision in another, adding a true cross-step dependency and model differentiation.
flags.spec_ref: Trajectory - Architectural Depth & Friction Exposure (fa6706f4)

flags.dimension: Tests - Redundancy
flags.reason: Confirmed in the test code: exactly one 1:1 overlap. flags.dimension: Rubric Criteria - Overall Rubric Quality - Major/Moderate
flags.reason: 6/18 criteria (33%) carry Moderate issues, far above the >15% (>=3) threshold. Four are non-atomic bundles (Not-Atomic-Minor = Moderate): idx1 bundles three board counts 'total pulled 24, failed bracket count 1, and additional weld-defect count 4' (opus pass 0.375 confirms lost discrimination); idx8 bundles 'return label/RMA, packaging or storage instructions, and vendor QC investigation status'; idx9 bundles recipient qa@interstatesupply.com + the same three requests; idx12 explicitly bundles two facts ('shows tracker status ... as Closed AND SEPARATELY shows the vendor return/QC workflow as needing follow-up'). Two are Overlapping/Redundant: idx15 'Project records are modified' (-3) is fully encompassed by idx14 'Airtable records are modified' (-3) because 'Katy Freeway Project' is itself an Airtable base/table (confirmed in server/data/airtable/data.json) — double-jeopardy on one action; idx7 'vendor follow-up needed' is encompassed by idx8 + idx12. Even the four non-atomic alone = 22% > 15%.
flags.fix: Split idx1 into 3 count criteria, idx8 into 3 content criteria, idx9 into a deterministic recipient check + 3 body-content criteria, and idx12 into 2 (tracker Closed / vendor follow-up needed). Drop idx15 (Project ⊆ Airtable) or re-scope it to a non-Airtable system; consolidate idx7 into idx8/idx12.
flags.spec_ref: V10_rubric.csv dim fa9dae99 (Overall Rubric Quality - Major/Moderate; >15% moderate-or-major = Fail); authoring_spec §9a Atomicity + appendix 'Rubric quality issue classifications' (Criteria Not Atomic-Minor & Overlapping/Redundant = Moderate)
